newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Rivals clash in Zaire ahead of new government.
newsitem.headline: Rivals clash in Zaire ahead of new government.

text.p: Supporters of two opposition leaders in Zaire clashed in the capital Kinshasa on Saturday, firing shots and throwing stones, witnesses said.

A spokesman for politician Frederic Kibassa Maliba said two bodyguards of Kibassa, who heads a breakaway faction of the opposition alliance led by former prime minister Etienne Tshisekedi, were wounded in the clash in Limete district.

Tension has been mounting in the capital since veteran President Mobutu Sese Seko returned this week from a long stay in Europe and has called for formation of a crisis government to deal with rebel fighting in eastern Zaire.

He appointed a new army chief and reorganised the military hierarchy to boost morale in his defeated army. But political bickering over who should head the government appeared to pose a new crisis away from the battlefront, political analysts said.
Mobutu was due to announce the new government on Saturday.
Tshisekedi's supporters have given a warning of trouble in Kinshasa if the radical opposition leader is not brought back to the position of prime minister that he held briefly.

"Supporters of Mr Tshisekedi arrived this morning at their party headquarters for a meeting. But they wanted to prevent Mr Kibassa's supporters from entering his (Kibassa's) house which is situated just next door," the spokesman, Prospere Ndume, told Reuters.
Witness Mubenga Amand said Kibassa's bodyguards responded by opening fire in the air.
As the 48-hour deadline set by Mobutu for the new government passed, there was still heated debate among political parties taking part in meetings on who should lead the cabinet.

Supporters of Kibassa's faction of the UDPS alliance of radical oppposition parties have put his name forward as a candidate. But incumbent Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo has support among many members of Mobutu's Popular Movement (MPR) who say Kengo represents stability, political sources said.
Other radical opposition groups and even some MPR members lined up behind Tshisekedi, who commands huge popularity among Kinshasa's teeeming population of urban poor, the sources said.
A meeting of the various groups scheduled to take place at midday on Saturday at Mobutu's barracks residence was postponed because of the deadlock, participants said.
The MPR's vice-president, Banza Mukalayi, said another two-day day extension to the deadline had been requested.

However Bemba Saolona, a closer ally of the president and head of the Zaire Business Association, said now that the deadline had passed it was up to Mobutu himself to announce the name of the prime minister.

Tshisekedi's UDPS has so far not taken part in the political party consultations initiated by Mobutu on Thursday, two days after returning home from four months of cancer surgery and rest in Europe. The president said he returned home to take charge and reverse the army's humiliation at the hands of Rwandan-backed rebels, who have seized land in two provinces.

"President Mobutu has promised to respond rapidly and positively to the hopes of the people. Even little children know that the prime minister the people are waiting for is Mr Tshisekedi," said Joseph Olengankoy, a radical MP of the Fonus Party allied to Tshiskedi.
"Imagine the anger of the population if he is not brought back. When they have made up their mind the people can be more powerful than an atomic bomb," Olengankoy told Reuters.

Since returning home Mobutu has shaken up the military high command. New chief of staff, the popular General Mahele Lieko Bokungu, has been awarded extended powers over the divided armed forces, including ability to call on units of the elite presidential guard to try and push back the rebels.
